name: to_markdown
description: Render a JSON document as markdown for a prompt to carry: an array of objects becomes a table, an object becomes its fields down the page, a list of values becomes a list. Costs fewer tokens than the same data as JSON, and gives a model something it can quote a row of.

data.description: The JSON document to render, usually a step's result: "{{ steps.rows.text }}". Pass this or path, not both.

path.description: A JSON file to read instead, relative to the workspace root. Must resolve inside it. Pass this or data, not both.

columns.description: Which fields become columns, and in which order. Only for an array of objects: without this they are the keys of the first row, and a row carrying a key the first row does not is refused. Naming a few of many is how a wide document becomes a table worth reading.

output_schema.description:
Markdown. An array of objects is a table with a header and a separator row. An object is a two-column table of field and value. An array of values is a "- " list. A pipe in a cell is escaped and a line break becomes
, so a row is always one line. null is an empty cell, and a nested value is compact JSON in its cell.

exit_codes.2: invalid input (stdin was not a JSON object, a parameter is the wrong type, or columns was passed for something that is not a table)
exit_codes.4: not permitted (path resolves outside the workspace root)
exit_codes.5: malformed data (the data is not JSON, or is a shape with no one rendering: a bare scalar, or an array mixing objects and values)
exit_codes.6: refused (a row carries a column the first row does not, or the array is empty and no columns were named)
